section_summary: This section (pages 161–238) of State Department decimal file 894.01B11 spans late November 1940 through March 1941, focusing primarily on reciprocal federal income tax exemptions under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Japanese government officials, military officers, technical experts, and university scholars stationed in or visiting the United States. It consists largely of diplomatic notes from the Japanese Embassy notifying the Department of State of personnel arrivals, travel itineraries, and departures, State Department reciprocal certifications to the Secretary of the Treasury, and Treasury acknowledgments directing Internal Revenue officials to facilitate tax exemptions and departure sailing permits. The file also includes interdepartmental intelligence transmittals regarding Japanese official travels, correspondence concerning a Japanese army inspector's attempt to tour American petroleum refineries, and administrative notifications regarding foreign official registration status.

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies to the Secretary of the Treasury that Dr. Tokio Sasaki is entitled to federal income tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.summary: Hull certifies to Treasury under Section 116(h) that Japan grants equivalent exemptions, covering Dr. Tokio Sasaki, studying in the US.

subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim notifies the Secretary of State of the scheduled departure from the United States of Yonosuke Tanaka.

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy requests income tax exemption for three Japanese officials stationed at the Japanese Government Railways office in New York.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 10 asks adding Railways secretaries Tembo and Obata and Tourist Board secretary Shoda to the exemption list. A duplicate is filed.

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Jiro Shoda.
subfiles.summary: Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) for Tembo, Obata and Shoda of the New York railway and tourist offices.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Jiro Shoda
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Japanese Note No. 10 concerning tax exemptions for three railway officials in New York.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Note No. 10 of January 18, 1941 on Tembo, Obata and Shoda and says a copy went to authorities.
